rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.2 (numbers serialized per ES6 Number.prototype.toString; 9007199254740993 is not exactly representable, rounds to 9007199254740992)
divergence_trap: Naive implementation that re-emits input number literals without reparsing outputs 9007199254740993
Naive implementation might preserve "-0" in output

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.2 (ES6 toString shortest decimal representation)
RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3 (solidus MAY be escaped but not required; canonical output uses unescaped)
divergence_trap: Naive implementation might output {"a":"hello\/world"} preserving the escape

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3 (characters U+0000 must be escaped as \u0000)
RFC 8785 Section 3.2.2.3 (strings serialized per ES6 JSON.stringify, preserving surrogate pairs)
divergence_trap: No divergence; ES6 compliant stringify produces same

rule: RFC 8785 Section 3.2.3 (keys sorted by UTF-16 code unit values; D83D < E000)
divergence_trap: Naive implementation sorting by Unicode code points would output {"\uE000":2,"\uD83D\uDE00":1}

rule: RFC 8785 does not define behavior for duplicate keys; implementations may reject or choose first occurrence
divergence_trap: Naive implementation might output {"a":2} (last wins) or reject
